title: Suraj Kund tank and its five temples
summary: An 18th-century water tank built by Jawahar Mal, ringed by five small temples. Locals still come at dawn; almost no tourist ever does. The steps on the north side are the original ones. Ten minutes from the Ghantaghar on foot.
location: Suraj Kund Road, near Ghantaghar, old Meerut
language: "Kund kithe hai?" — Where is the tank? (Haryanvi-Khari boli mix heard here)
tips: It is a place of worship for the neighbourhood, not a photo studio. Remove shoes at the temple platforms and do not put feet in the water.

title: The bat-pressing workshops of Sports Colony
summary: Meerut makes a large share of India's cricket bats, and a handful of family workshops in Sports Colony still cleft, press and hand-splice willow in the open. Most will let you watch for a few minutes if you ask. The best time is mid-morning when the presses run.
location: Sports Colony / Victoria Park side, Meerut
language: "Thoda dekh sakte hain?" — May we watch for a bit?
tips: Ask the owner first, stay clear of the presses, and if you buy, buy from the workshop rather than a showroom so the maker gets the margin.

title: Raniji ki Baori and the 50 forgotten stepwells
summary: Bundi has more than fifty stepwells inside the old town, and Raniji ki Baori from 1699 is the finest — 46 metres deep with carved elephant brackets. Kipling wrote about this town. Most visitors go to Jaipur instead and miss all of it.
location: Inside the walled town, five minutes from Nawal Sagar
language: "Baori kitthe hai sa?" — Where is the stepwell? (Hadoti)
tips: Several baoris are locked; the ASI caretaker opens them on request. Do not climb down wet steps in monsoon.

title: Theyyam season in the northern kavus
summary: From December to April, sacred groves across Kasaragod host Theyyam — a ritual where the performer, usually from a historically oppressed community, becomes the deity and blesses the village. It is not a stage show; there is no ticket. Village temples publish their kaliyattam dates locally.
location: Kavus around Nileshwar, Cherukunnu and Kanhangad
bestTime: December to April, mostly through the night
tips: Ask the temple committee before photographing. Do not use flash, do not stand in the deity's path, and dress modestly. Offer to the temple, never to the performer mid-ritual.

title: The Ahom maidams that nobody visits
summary: Sivasagar was the Ahom capital for six centuries. Rang Ghar, Talatal Ghar and the Shivadol tank are known, but the burial mounds — maidams — in the surrounding fields are extraordinary and empty. Charaideo, an hour away, was inscribed by UNESCO in 2024.
location: Sivasagar town and Charaideo, 28 km away
tips: The maidams are burial sites; do not climb the mounds. Hire a local guide from the Sivasagar museum rather than a car tout.
